Threat.value: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Memory.value: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me

I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me
I can no longer trust my own body

vignette:
Ifeoma, a 42-year-old factory worker, had been living in a world that felt increasingly perilous ever since the day her life took a harrowing turn. It was a sweltering afternoon when she was abducted from a local market. The memory of that day played on a loop in her mind, vivid yet surreal-like a nightmare that refused to let go. Ifeoma could still recall the oppressive heat, the scent of spices lingering in the air, and the sense of normalcy shattered in an instant. Stripped of her autonomy and subjected to unspeakable acts, she had emerged from that experience with scars that ran deeper than the flesh.

In the months that followed, Ifeoma found herself trapped in a relentless cycle of hyper-vigilance and avoidance. She had come to believe that the world was a dangerous place, where her safety was an illusion. Ordinary sounds, the creak of a door, the rustle of leaves, would send her heart racing, her body reacting before her mind could catch up. Ifeoma would jump at the slightest noise, a reaction that left her feeling ashamed and isolated. The factory, once a place of camaraderie, now felt like a minefield. She would sit at her station, listening intently for any sounds that might indicate an intruder, her focus split between the assembly line and the growing anxiety in her chest.

To cope, Ifeoma developed a series of maladaptive strategies that helped her navigate daily life but also wove a web of isolation around her. Heavy makeup became a mask-if she could cover the turmoil beneath her skin, perhaps no one would see the fear in her eyes. She spent hours perfecting her appearance, using it as a shield against the world. Yet, deep down, she knew it was a temporary fix; the heaviness of the makeup only reminded her of the weight of her trauma. 

At home, she surrounded herself with distractions. Television blared in the background, books lay open on her lap, and her mind raced with thoughts of trivial matters. She kept herself busy, believing that if she occupied her mind, the memories would fade. But they never did. They lingered like ghosts, always just beneath the surface, ready to engulf her in a moment of stillness. Ifeoma avoided wearing clothes she used to love-bright patterns and flowing fabrics that reminded her of a time when she felt free and confident. Instead, she opted for drab, loose-fitting attire, hoping to blend into the background and avoid drawing attention to herself.

The weather also played tricks on her mind. On particularly hot and humid days, she would find herself paralyzed by memories of that fateful afternoon. The sun felt like a spotlight, reminding her of the oppressive heat she had endured. She would retreat into her apartment, curtains drawn, as if shielding herself from the elements could also shield her from the memories that clawed at her insides.

Ifeoma's sense of self eroded over time. She felt no longer capable of doing the things that once defined her-no longer the vibrant, sociable woman she had been before the trauma. Her body, once a source of strength, now felt unreliable, betraying her at the most inconvenient moments. She would catch herself staring in the mirror, grappling with the notion that the reflection before her was of someone unrecognizable. The memory of the torture felt alien, as if it had happened to another person entirely, and she often questioned whether it was real.

It wasn't until a particularly challenging day at work, when a colleague innocently called her name, that the dam finally broke. The familiar sound echoed in her mind, triggering a flood of memories and emotions that overwhelmed her. She found herself retreating to the restroom, tears spilling down her cheeks, gasping for breath as she fought against the wave of panic. It was that moment of vulnerability that led Ifeoma to seek help, realizing that she could no longer navigate this labyrinth of fear alone. She hoped for relief, for a way to reclaim her life, but what frightened her most was the prospect of confronting the very memories she had spent so long trying to bury.
